issues.description: IdentityGrammar admits unary minus on values that semantically cannot be negative
issues.detail: The grammar now wraps both numeric literals in IDENTITY(seed, increment) with an optional SignedSegmentGrammar. The stated motivation is negative seeds, yet the second argument — the increment — is also opened to a sign. SQL Server forbids a zero increment and the seed/increment distinction is meaningful; conflating them in the grammar removes a property the parser previously enforced. State the precondition for each operand separately, or accept that you have weakened the specification of IdentityGrammar in exchange for one valid case. This is structured-programming hygiene: do not loosen an invariant farther than the bug requires.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor silently drops the multi-action delimited form
issues.detail: The previous grammar wrapped the action list in Delimited(OneOf(...)), permitting `ALTER TABLE t ADD ..., DROP COLUMN ..., DROP COLUMN ...` in a single statement. The new grammar replaces the outer Delimited with a bare OneOf, so each ALTER TABLE statement now accepts exactly one action. The deleted fixture (column_b ADD + two DROP COLUMNs comma-delimited) is precisely such a case, and the PR removes it on the grounds that it is 'invalid' — but T-SQL does in fact permit a single ADD followed by comma-separated columns, and the previous tests asserted exactly this shape. The author has not stated the precondition this change asserts; the diff narrows the accepted language without proof that the removed inputs are illegal in T-SQL. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no stated rationale
issues.detail: The _default_language grammar gains NumericLiteralSegment as an alternative alongside quoted literal and naked identifier. The PR description mentions only 'non-quoted identifier' for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE. If language IDs (lcid) are intended, say so; if not, this is grammar widening by accident. Either the postcondition should be tightened or the rationale should be documented. A reviewer should not have to guess the precondition.

issues.description: No negative test for the now-rejected multi-action ALTER TABLE
issues.detail: If the multi-action ALTER TABLE form is genuinely invalid T-SQL — the implicit claim made by deleting the fixture and removing the outer Delimited — then a parse-failure fixture should assert it remains rejected. Otherwise a future refactor could silently reintroduce the broader grammar without any test catching it. Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence; here there is not even a test.

issues.description: New fixtures exercise the happy path only; no boundary cases
issues.detail: The added fixtures cover one shape per feature: one table variable index, one CREATE LOGIN with all three new forms at once, one negative seed (INT_MIN), one multi-DROP COLUMN, one multi-DROP CONSTRAINT. There are no cases with mixed positive/negative increment, no DROP that mixes CONSTRAINT and COLUMN in one statement (which the new grammar happens not to allow — make that explicit), no DEFAULT_DATABASE as a delimited-identifier, and no PASSWORD with the bare N prefix alone. The fixtures demonstrate the presence of correct behavior on the chosen inputs; they do not establish the boundary of the accepted language.

review.summary: The PR widens four T-SQL grammar productions and adds happy-path fixtures, but in two places it changes the accepted language without stating the new specification. The IDENTITY grammar now admits a unary minus on the increment as well as the seed, which is broader than the stated bug. The ALTER TABLE refactor replaces an outer Delimited(OneOf(...)) with a bare OneOf, narrowing the accepted statement to a single action and deleting a previously valid fixture as 'invalid' without proof. TESTED-NOT-PROVED on both: the author has not articulated the pre/postcondition each grammar now enforces, and there are no negative tests asserting the new boundary. The CREATE LOGIN and table-variable-index additions are mechanically reasonable, though DEFAULT_LANGUAGE quietly gains NumericLiteralSegment with no stated rationale. Verdict: REASONED in parts, UNREASONED in the ALTER TABLE and IDENTITY changes; the diff should not land until the specifications it implies are stated and tested at their boundaries.
